# gitmoap_repository_providers (Data Source)

List the providers in effect for a repository. What the repository's pipelines may use. A repository has no provider settings of its own, so this resolves those of its group and every group above it, the nearest setting deciding: whether it is enabled, the version pinned and the versions allowed, whether it follows the latest version and a newer one is published, and whether the organization's policy accepts its tier. Each entry says where it was set; for a setting made at a group you cannot see, who made it and where are withheld. Anyone who can see the repository; on a public repository that includes callers who are not signed in.

The token needs `provider_settings:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_providers" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository id

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `allowed_versions` (Attributes) The set of versions a node may declare for a provider at a scope.

`AnyPublished` (the default when unset) permits every catalogued version —
the trust boundary is the catalog. `List`/`Range` let an org curate. The
version a node *runs* is always an exact `ProviderVersion`; a `Range` only
governs which exact versions are declarable, so reproducibility holds (no
floating run-time versions).

`kind` says which applies: `any_published`; `list`, with `versions`; `range`, with `max`, `min`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--allowed_versions))
- `default_version` (String)
- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `inherited` (Boolean)
- `installed_at` (String)
- `installed_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--installed_by))
- `latest_lifecycle_state` (String) Lifecycle state of a published `ProviderVersionManifest`. `Active` is the
default; `Deprecated` still runs but the trigger-time validator surfaces a
warning; `Sunset` runs only inside its grace window, after which a trigger
referencing it fails validation.
- `latest_version` (String)
- `override_parent` (Boolean)
- `owning_group_id` (String)
- `provider_id` (String)
- `provider_tier` (String) How a pipeline provider is distributed and how much it is vouched for.
- `publisher_verified` (Boolean) Whether the owning publisher's namespace is verified.
- `source_scope_id` (String)
- `source_scope_type` (String)
- `tier_accepted` (Boolean) Whether the provider's tier is accepted by the resolved per-org policy.
- `track_latest` (Boolean) Whether this install tracks the provider's latest published version.
When `true`, an unpinned node resolves to `latest_version` at trigger.
- `update_available` (Boolean) Whether a newer version than the install's `default_version` is published
— a pure semver compare that never mutates the install (D5 K6).

<a id="nestedatt--items--allowed_versions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.allowed_versions`

Read-Only:

- `kind` (String)
- `max` (String)
- `min` (String)
- `versions` (List of String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--installed_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.installed_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
